newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks end week on another record close.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks end week on another record close.

text.p: 10yrbond futs 92.335 +0.155 Gold 342.40/90 Lon fix 343.75
*Stocks end record-breaking week with closing high, boosted by strong metal prices. Vol 357.45 million, value A$881.70 million, 1,064 stocks traded, 340 steady, 456 up, 268 down.
The Australian share market topped off a record breaking week with a new record close on Friday aided by stronger metal prices which boosting resource sector and set off active trade in BHP.
Banks continued to rally.
The All Ordinaries index ended 21.3points up at 2,526.0, breaking the previous record close of 2,517.6 set on Wednesday, but off the intra-day record of 2,258.1 set in afternoon trade.
The June share price index futures also ended at a robust 2,539, up 24 points, widening the premium to the physical stocks to 13 points from 10 points around the midsession.
Brokers said the market was also boosted by a rally in the bond market on after comments by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan and a jump in the S&P500 futures contract.
"It's up on the back of a better resources market," said Chris Walker, head of Australian equities at fund manager Colonial Investment Management.
There was also good support for other major miners CRA, Pasminco and WMC following strong gains for metal prices on the LME, brokers said.
Gold stocks were also stronger as gold in Hong Kong extended gains from New York's higher close.

Brokers said the rally in the bond market underpinned the enduring rise in the market's biggest sector, the bank index as expectations of a good set of half yearly results from Westpac and NAB when they report next week.
"Greenspan spoke, the boys got all hot. The S&P is up quite strongly on Globex, bonds are up quite strongly so we are obviously looking for a bit of improvement in the offshore markets," Walker said.
The All Ordinaries has had trouble staying above the 2,500 level until this week. "It has had resistance at 2,500 before, but today it is quite happy to stay up here," Walker said.
The market surge helped ICI Australia recover some of Thursday's losses following news that its British parent ICI Plc plans to sell its A$2.0 billion controlling stake.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures trading was quieter, while their was renewed interest in options trade.
Contracts traded 5,506 (6,550)
Total options traded 44,377 (38,518).
In other market news, long dated Australian bond yields dropped to the lowest level since late February, prompted by shortcovering after an unusally marked move in U.S. debt on comments by Greenspan.
At 5.30 p.m. (0730 GMT), the 10 year T-bond yield was down 14 basis points to 7.66 percent yield.
Australian dollar unwound overnight gains against U.S. dollar and continued to weaken against the yen on Friday, caught up in U.S. dollar weakness and outright selling against the yen.

At 5.30 p.m., the dollar was trading at US$0.7779/84, just up on Thursday's local close of US$0.7776/81. --------------------------(TECHNICALS)-------------------------- Short-term range Support Restnce RSI-14 MA-10 MA-20
